messages:
ajay: quick heads-up — Orca Health (large telco customer) is pushing for p95=80ms / p99=200ms on the chat endpoint. Sales asked if engineering can commit this week.
maria: woof. current canary numbers are nowhere near that at our requested QPS. we saw p95 ~= 92ms, p99 ~= 310ms at 30 qps with microbatch=8. tail dominated by warmups.
kevin: confirmed. I dug into profiling — two big tail drivers: kernel swap on rare long sequences, and KV cache cold misses that cascade into extra token latency. quick dump:
```
canary @ 30 QPS, microbatch=8:
  p50 45ms
  p95 92ms
  p99 310ms
  root causes:
    - KV miss rate ~12% on first token -> +80-120ms for those requests
    - kernel selection fallback when seq_len > 1024 -> +35-60ms
    - microbatching adds headroom but increases burst tail
```
maria: tl;dr: we can hit p95 target by tuning, p99 is expensive to guarantee unless we carve out low-latency capacity or change routing/kv behavior.
tom_sales: Orca said they're willing to pay for a latency tier if it gets them SLAs. they'd prefer not to pay double, but will accept a premium.
ana_product: @maria @kevin need a short tradeoff doc for product + pricing. what are our concrete levers and expected delta? Product wants to present options to Orca by EOD Friday.
kevin: options (short):
  1) microbatch -> 4 (reduce queueing): proj p95 ~78-85ms, p99 ~230-280ms, cost +12-18% (more effective GPU ops lost)
  2) prewarm KV for known prefixes / customer pinned keys: proj p99 drop ~100ms on warm misses, operational complexity + cache warmup policy
  3) low-latency lane (small microbatch, kernel pinned, reserved capacity): p95 ~60-75ms, p99 ~150-200ms, cost +35-60% (reserved GPU)
  4) fallback model variant (faster quantized kernel) for high-latency requests: p95 similar, p99 better for some workloads but quality risk
maria: also a near-term mitigation: aggressive KV TTL and routing warmups for session-based traffic. that helps if Orca's traffic is sticky.
tom_sales: Orca traffic is sessiony (chat assistants), so KV prewarm seems attractive to them.
ajay: schedule-wise: can we implement microbatch change + KV prewarm toggle as a config flag in 3 days for canary? and a low-latency lane plan in 2 sprints?
kevin: microbatch toggle is trivial (config + perf test) — can get canary in 48-72h. KV prewarm needs a small routing hook + metrics but doable in 3 days for a canary experiment.
maria: kernel pinning for priority lane requires infra changes (kernel cache pinning across model variants) — that's 2 sprints.
ana_product: for the customer pitch, propose 2 tiers:
  - Standard: p95 SLA 100ms, p99 best-effort
  - Low-latency: p95 80-90ms, p99 220-260ms (reserved or premium routing + KV prewarm)
  Sales can offer a 90-day intro price for Orca if we commit to roadmaps.
tom_sales: Orca agrees to trial low-latency tier if we can hit p95 <=90ms and p99 <=250ms for the first 30 days. they'll sign a 6-month reserved commitment if results look good.
kevin: quick projection with microbatch=4 + KV prewarm + light kernel pinning heuristics:
```
projection (canary):
  p50 ~42ms
  p95 ~82ms
  p99 ~245ms
```
kevin: note uncertainty +/- 10-15% on p99 depending on sequence distribution and cold-starts.
ajay: propose we accept the Orca trial terms: target p95<=90ms p99<=250ms for 30-day trial. action items:
  - eng: microbatch toggle to 4 + canary (kevin/maria) — 72h
  - eng: KV prewarm routing flag canary (kevin) — 72h
  - eng-infra: plan for reserved low-latency lane (maria) — 2 sprints
  - product/sales: publish offer + terms (ana/tom) — EOD Fri
perf-bot: creating perf dashboard for Orca trial: /dash/eng-runtime/orca-trial
perf-bot: projection summary added to dashboard: p95 target 90ms, p99 target 250ms, baseline p99=310ms
maria: ack. I'll run a deterministic perf sweep and post updated numbers in this thread when canary results are in.
ajay: thanks all. standard caveat: if canary shows p99 > 270ms we'll pause trial and do kernel-level fixes. :thumbsup:
kevin: noting follow-ups: logs -> trace ids for KV misses, add histogram of kernel selection events, and tag Orca requests for routing visibility.
tom_sales: I'll tell Orca the plan and get them to sign the trial terms. will update after legal call.
ana_product: good compromise. product OK with the phased approach.
perf-bot: scheduled canary run in 12h, will post results here as soon as available.
